settings.title: Homey Toolkit
settings.subtitle: App Settings

email.title: Email settings
email.intro: Configure Gmail to send email from a Homey Flow.
email.instructions: Use a Google app password, not your regular Google account password. App passwords require 2-Step Verification.
email.flowInstructions: After saving these settings, use the “Send an email with Gmail” action card in a Flow. Connect it to an HTTP API trigger to send an email when a request is received.
email.securityNote: The app password is stored in Homey settings. Keep API token authentication enabled if email sending can be triggered through the HTTP API.
email.appPasswordHint: Leave blank to keep the saved password.
email.addressRequired: Enter a Gmail address before saving.
email.testSuccess: Test email sent. Check your Gmail inbox.

ical.title: iCal calendars
ical.intro: Add calendar URLs to synchronize events and use them in Homey Flows.
ical.privacy: Calendar URLs may contain private access tokens. Store them securely and do not share them.
ical.googleHelp: Google Calendar: copy the Secret address in iCal format from the calendar settings.
ical.outlookHelp: Outlook: publish the calendar and copy its ICS link.
ical.icloudHelp: iCloud: enable Public Calendar and use the original link. Apple's default Home and Work calendars do not provide public links.
ical.flowInfo: Use the iCal Flow cards to sync calendars, create local events, and trigger automations when events start or end.
ical.invalidCalendar: Calendar name or URL is invalid.
ical.invalidInterval: Sync interval must be between 5 and 1,440 minutes.
ical.invalidDays: Sync timeframe must be between 1 and 365 days.

api.title: Using the API
api.intro: Use the trigger card in Advanced Flow to register a route and HTTP method.
api.routeText: The leading slash is optional. informatie and /informatie refer to the same route.
api.methodsText: Use POST, PUT, and PATCH for JSON data. Use GET to retrieve data and DELETE to remove an action or resource.
api.responseText: Use the Respond with... action card to send a JSON response, or Respond with 200 for a simple confirmation.
api.fieldText: Add ?field= to a GET request to read one property from the Flow response. ?veld= is also supported. The property may be directly in the response or inside data.

countdown.title: Countdown timers
countdown.intro: Create timers here, set their duration in seconds, then select them in the countdown flow cards. The start/reset cards use this duration.
countdown.activeEmpty: There are no active countdown timers.
countdown.activeLoadFailed: Could not load active countdown timers.
countdown.invalidName: Timer names must contain between 1 and 80 characters.
countdown.invalidDuration: Duration must be a positive whole number of seconds.
countdown.invalidImport: The timer file does not contain a valid timer list.
countdown.importFailed: Could not read the timer export file.

information.title: How the API settings work
information.intro: Configure the local HTTP server here. Changes are applied after saving; Homey may indicate that a restart is required.
information.serverText: Port determines where the API listens. CORS controls whether browser clients may make cross-origin requests. Access-Control-Allow-Origin limits which origin is allowed when CORS is enabled.
information.routesText: Create a trigger flow with a route such as informatie and select its HTTP method. A leading slash is optional, so informatie and /informatie are equivalent.
information.methodsText: Supported methods are GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS. POST, PUT, and PATCH can receive JSON in the request body.
information.tokenText: Enable token authentication and generate a token. The recommended method is the Authorization header. For simple URL clients, add the token as shown below.
information.headerText: The token is checked before a Homey flow starts. Generating a new token invalidates the old token. Do not share the token or expose the API port directly to the public internet.

examples.title: Request examples
examples.intro: Register the route and method in an Advanced Flow trigger, then use one of these requests from a client or HomeyScript.
examples.get4: Read a single value from the response.
examples.head1: Check whether an endpoint is available without downloading its response.
examples.head2: Check whether a device endpoint exists.
examples.head3: Check whether the API is reachable.
examples.options1: Ask which HTTP methods are available for a route.
examples.options3: Inspect the allowed methods before integrating a client.
examples.tokenNote: When authentication is enabled, add ?token=abc to the URL or use Authorization: Bearer abc. POST, PUT, and PATCH bodies must contain valid JSON.
